scenes.tts: Does a mouse react more to a gentle puff of air because of its brain, or because of the first neuron in the pathway? The authors asked this in mouse lines carrying mutations in genes associated with autism in people. The puff was fixed: zero point nine P S I, for fifty milliseconds, on back hairy skin. The measure was the size of a startle-like movement. All four mouse lines reacted more strongly than controls.

scenes.tts: Then came the restriction. Advillin Cree supplies Cree recombinase to peripheral sensory neurons. That means dorsal root and trigeminal neurons, plus sympathetic ganglion neurons, not one subtype. Crossed to a floxed allele, it removes that gene from those cells. The brain keeps its copy. The team did this for two genes, M E C P two and G A B R B three.

The team did this for two genes, Mecp2 and Gabrb3.

scenes.tts: Deleting M E C P two or G A B R B three from peripheral neurons alone, with the brain left intact, was sufficient for stronger air puff responses. Developmental deletion also caused anxiety-like and social-interaction differences, in the assays tested. Sufficient does not mean it is the whole story.

scenes.tts: The reverse test restored M E C P two mainly in peripheral sensory neurons, on an otherwise null background. The driver also reaches sympathetic ganglion neurons. Tactile sensitivity was rescued, and so were selected anxiety-like and social measures. Lethality, memory deficits and motor deficits were not rescued. So the peripheral neuron explains part of the phenotype, and not the rest.

scenes.tts: In mouse dorsal horn, G A B R B three containing GABA A receptors sit on the central terminals of A beta and A delta low threshold mechanoreceptor afferents. In sensory neuron M E C P two mutants, puncta next to V Glut one terminals were reduced by about seventy per cent, counted in fixed tissue. The authors attributed the touch phenotype to deficient GABA A presynaptic inhibition. The study reads GABA depolarisation as reducing release. Work in proprioceptive afferents instead finds GABA A aiding spike propagation.
scenes.caption: In mouse dorsal horn, GABRB3-containing GABA-A receptors sit on the central terminals of Aβ and Aδ low-threshold mechanoreceptor afferents. In sensory-neuron Mecp2 mutants, puncta next to VGlut1 terminals were reduced by about 70 per cent, counted in fixed tissue. The authors attributed the touch phenotype to deficient GABA-A presynaptic inhibition. The study reads GABA depolarisation as reducing release. Work in proprioceptive afferents instead finds GABA-A aiding spike propagation.

scenes.tts: One model does not fit that account. In cultured large dorsal root ganglion neurons from Shank three mutants, I h was reduced and excitability was higher. No altered G A B R B three was detected at the terminals. Same behaviour, different cellular defect. These are sufficiency tests in one species, and the behaviours are assays, not experiences. Keep the rule: in these mouse models, part of a tactile phenotype can begin outside the brain.
